Czyzew New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Czyżew, Poland

Not demolished. Czyżew, founded in 1476 and confirmed with town rights by King August III in 1738, had an early Jewish community (over 200 by the town-rights confirmation) initially subordinate to Węgrów's kehilla until likely the late 18th century. Jewish population reached 97% (1,441) after an 1857 railway connection spurred growth, settling at 87% (1,595) by 1921; a local tzitzit factory exported ritual garments primarily eastward. In 1941, roughly 5,000 people - including many Czyżew Jews - were massacred in a mass execution near Mianówek forest; the town's ghetto, liquidated in November 1942, sent remaining residents to Treblinka. This second Jewish cemetery, established around 1820, was largely destroyed for building material during and after WWII; the Mianówek murder site was separately commemorated with a granite monument in 1959.
